newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks drop as bank, finance sales continue.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks drop as bank, finance sales continue.

text.p: Selling of major bank stocks and blue chip finance, property and communications shares sparked a further sharp fall in the Thai stock market early on Wednesday morning, traders said.
The composite SET Index fell 14.18 points, or 2.20 percent, to 629.10 by 0351 GMT. The SET 50 lost 1.16 points, or 2.45 percent to 46.19 on trade worth 570 million baht.

Leading bank stocks, largely immune to a 2.55 percent fall in the market on Tuesday, were also sold on Wednesday as investors are fearful that lower economic growth prospects will translate into flatter earnings growth.
The bourse closed at a 5-1/2 year low on Tuesday but big bank stocks were trading at a premium to previous year lows.

The finance sector lost another 3.87 percent. Doubts surrounding the progress of mergers in the sector, and the quality of the combined property and hire purchase exposures of even some leading companies are spooking investors, traders said.

The exposure of some leading finance firms to the hire purchase and property sectors combined is over 40 percent and there are increasing worries among investors about hire purchase loans particularly for cars, analysts said.
Property loans are already widely considered problematic as the market faces serious oversupply and declining prices in most sectors. Property stocks lost 3.60 percent by mid-morning.

Communications shares were also heavily sold. Mobile phone operator Advanced Info Services Plc shed nine baht to 151. Investors fear government plans to grant new licences and introduce competition may hurt earnings, traders said.
